title: A Full-Stack Framework for Rail Freight Digitalization: Towards Energy-Aware Data Sovereignty
content: Rail freight digitalization is limited because wagons have no power supply and stakeholders are reluctant to share operational data. This paper presents a full-stack framework that connects ultra-low-power Internet of Things (IoT) devices on the wagon with a sovereign Federated Data Space (FDS). Wireless Sensor Nodes (WSENs) send data to a Wireless On-board Unit Coordinator (WOBUC), which forwards them to the cloud over Long Term Evolution for Machines (LTE-M) or Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT). The measured energy cost of each task was used to build a battery-life simulator, with average-current errors below 3.5%. In highway tests with one transmission per minute, the median active radio time increased by 156% for NB-IoT and by 6.8% for LTE-M compared with static tests, and NB-IoT reconnected less reliably after base-station changes. Simulations project several years of battery life for the WSENs. For the WOBUC, sensing every 5 min and transmitting once a day over LTE-M with Power Saving Mode (PSM) gives a projected 606 days, compared with less than a week when each 1-min cycle is sent directly. The framework also proposes using predicted battery life to set the duration of FDS data-access contracts. It was tested in a freight yard within the Europe’s Rail FP5-TRANS4M-R project.
